summary: Hotdesk switch port-security on bridge VLAN intermittently blocks WireGuard peers leading to IP rebinds
description: Users in the SF hotdesk area reported repeated WireGuard disconnects and inability to reach internal services. Affected clients retained an IP for a short period, then the local address changed and WireGuard reported peer unreachable. Multiple devices across adjacent ports were impacted. Initial triage suggested a VPN/client issue but symptoms pointed to layer 2 instability on the access switch feeding the hotdesk bridge VLAN.
impact: Multiple engineers at the SF hotdesk (approx 12 seats) experienced frequent VPN drops and intermittent internal service access over an 8-hour window. Productivity impacted for hotdesk users; no org-wide impact. Automated synthetic checks for the hotdesk subrange showed elevated ARP/cache churn.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect a laptop to any port in the hotdesk bay (ports 41-52 on switch sw-sf-hotdesk-01)
2) Join corporate Wi-Fi (corp-net), ensure split-tunnel WireGuard config is active and route default via local ISP not over VPN
3) Start a WireGuard session to the Redwood internal Gateway (wg01), leave idle for ~2-5 minutes
4) Attempt to access an internal service (git, jira) or tail logs over SSH; observe dropped sessions and new local IP allocation or ARP timeout messages
5) On the switch, run 'show mac address-table' and 'show arp' to observe MAC flapping or duplicate entries tied to the hotdesk VLAN
logs: Client WireGuard log (macOS): 'peer wg01 unreachable, handshake timeout', followed by 'replaced local address 10.10.55.24 -> 10.10.55.234'
DHCP server logs: lease for 10.10.55.24 assigned, then released 45s later with client MAC still present on switch but different port
Switch syslog (sw-sf-hotdesk-01): 'Port 46 security violation: MAC address limit exceeded', 'STP topology change on VLAN 210 detected on Gi1/0/46'
Network edge logs: 'ARP storm detected for subnet 10.10.55.0/24, suppressed 120s'
investigation_notes: 03/08 09:25 - CS observed repeated WireGuard drop reports from 3 users. Triage: confirm scope and reproduce.
03/08 10:00 - SRE captured switch syslog showing 'security violation' events on several hotdesk ports. Not all affected ports raised alarms simultaneously.
03/08 11:15 - Reproduced locally. 'show mac address-table dynamic' showed the same MAC moving between Gi1/0/45 and Gi1/0/46, then cleared by port-security.

03/08 12:00 - Hypothesis: port-security with sticky MAC or low max-mac setting plus edge mis-wired patch caused MAC flapping; STP topology changes triggered transient blackholing and DHCP rebinds leading to WireGuard re-handshakes.
03/08 13:30 - Verified patch panel: ports 46/47 were connected to a temporary unmanaged patch leading to duplicate L2 path during desk reconfiguration (hotdesk moves).

03/09 09:20 - Confirmed DHCP snooping and port-security interaction: when port-security triggered a violation, the switch shut the port for a short time (err-disabled) and the DHCP lease was released, causing clients to get a new IP on reconnection and WireGuard to rebind.
03/09 10:00 - Scoped: only ports in hotdesk bay VLAN 210; other office areas not impacted. No software bug in WireGuard detected.
03/10 15:45 - Mitigation applied: disabled port-security enforcement on the victim ports and removed the rogue patch cable. Monitored for 48 hours; ARP churn subsided.
03/11 09:00 - Permanent fix scheduled: update switch template to increase max-mac for hotdesk ports to 8, enable BPDU Guard, and add patch panel labeling to avoid future ad-hoc cross-connects.
Reference artifacts: Slack #infra-sf thread (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/INFRA-SF/p03Jq1x), Confluence runbook 'sw-hotdesk-port-template' (https://confluence.redwood/infra/switching/hotdesk)

resolution: Mitigation: removed rogue patch cable and temporarily relaxed port-security on hotdesk access ports to prevent err-disabled state. Permanent remediation: template change applied to sw-sf-hotdesk-01 and sibling switches - increased max-mac to 8, BPDU Guard enabled, DHCP snooping binding table validation added, and updated patch panel labeling/process. Communicated change to Facilities. Change PR: github.com/redwood-infra/switch-configs/pulls/87. No firmware upgrade required.
